verified_excerpt: The US-ANSI keyboard layout (ANSI-INCITS 154-1988) has a horizontal Return key with the \ key above it. It is often 2.25u wide.
The ISO standard (ISO/IEC 9995-2) mandates a vertical Return key spanning two rows. The Japanese JIS standard (JIS X 6002-1980) uses the same key as ISO. It is often 1.25u wide.

A "backwards-L shaped" (or just "L-shaped") Return key is the union of the ISO and ANSI Return keys. The key is often called Big-ass Enter because of its size, or Asian enter because it is found on many East Asian keyboards.

PC keyboards using the ANSI layout as used by the IBM Model M are typically referred to as 101-key (pre-1995), 104-key (with the Windows and context menu keys added), and 87-key (standard tenkeyless layout).

verified_excerpt: Physical format is separate from language layout. ANSI, ISO, JIS and ABNT describe a keyboard’s shape and key count, not the software language assigned to it. An ISO keyboard body can carry a QWERTY layout just as easily as a QWERTZ one.

European languages have adapted the core arrangement to accommodate characters absent from the 26-letter English alphabet. Some variants add physical keys, while others use the AltGr key for accented or specialised characters
